title: Quebec expressions set 1
goal: By the end of this lesson you can understand and use a first set of everyday Quebec expressions (c'est correct, pantoute, tiguidou, magasiner, être tanné, c'est plate, jaser…), know their standard equivalents, and judge when each one fits.

learn.h: Saying OK: c'est correct and tiguidou
body: *C'est correct* is the Quebec 'it's OK / that's fine / no problem'. It's neutral and used everywhere: *Je suis en retard. — C'est correct!* In France it would be *Ce n'est pas grave* or *D'accord*. It does not mean 'that's right' (which is *C'est ça* or *Exact*).
*Tiguidou* means 'perfect, all good'. It's playful, a bit old-fashioned, and always friendly: *On se voit à huit heures? — Tiguidou!*
*Ça marche* and *Parfait* are neutral and work everywhere too.
learn.tip: C'est correct = it's fine, not 'that's correct'.

body: *Pantoute* is the Quebec form of *pas du tout* (not at all). It's informal and strong: *T'es fâché? — Pantoute!* (Mad? Not at all!) *J'comprends pantoute.* (I don't understand at all.)
It can stand alone as an answer or follow a verb, just like *pas du tout*.

learn.h: Feelings: être tanné, c'est plate, avoir hâte
body: *Être tanné (de)* = to be fed up (with): *Je suis tanné de l'hiver!* Standard: *en avoir assez*, *en avoir marre* (France).
*C'est plate* = it's boring, it's too bad: *Le film est plate.* *C'est plate, il pleut.* Standard: *C'est ennuyeux. / C'est dommage.*
*Avoir hâte (à / de)* = to look forward to, can't wait: *J'ai hâte aux vacances!* This one is standard French too (France prefers *avoir hâte de*).

learn.h: Doing things: magasiner, jaser, avoir de la misère
body: *Magasiner* = to go shopping (from *magasin*). It's a regular -er verb and fully accepted in Quebec, even in ads: *On magasine samedi?* France says *faire du shopping* or *faire les magasins*.
*Jaser* = to chat: *On jase!* (We're just chatting.) *Avoir de la misère (à)* = to have a hard time: *J'ai de la misère à comprendre.* (standard: *J'ai du mal à…*)

*C'est correct*, *magasiner*, *jaser* and *avoir hâte* are fine with almost anyone, even at work. *Pantoute*, *tanné*, *plate*, *brûlé* and *avoir de la misère* are informal: perfect with friends, colleagues and neighbours, less so in a job interview or formal email.
Using them well makes you sound local; overusing them in formal settings sounds odd. The standard equivalents always work.

examples.fr: Je suis en retard, désolé! — C'est correct.
Es-tu correct? Tu as l'air fatigué.
examples.en: Are you OK? You look tired.

examples.fr: On se voit à huit heures? — Tiguidou!
Je ne comprends pas du tout. / J'comprends pantoute.

examples.en: Are you mad? — Not at all!
The kids are tired of waiting.

examples.fr: C'est plate, il pleut pour la fête.
examples.en: It's too bad, it's raining for the party.
I can't wait for the holidays!
Shall we go shopping on Saturday?
She's shopping around for a new car.

examples.fr: On jase au café après le travail.
examples.en: We chat at the café after work.

examples.fr: J'ai de la misère à me lever le matin.
examples.en: I have a hard time getting up in the morning.

examples.fr: Je suis brûlé après la semaine.

quebec.intro: This lesson IS the Quebec layer: c'est correct, pantoute, tiguidou, magasiner and être tanné, plus a few close cousins. Learn each one with its standard equivalent so you can switch registers.

items.note: friendly, a bit old-fashioned and playful

items.std: faire du shopping / faire les magasins

drills.why: In Quebec, c'est correct = it's fine.
Être tanné = to be fed up.

drills.q: Which is fine in a formal email?
drills.why: Avoir hâte de is standard French.

drills.en: Shall we go shopping on Saturday?
drills.why: magasiner is a regular -er verb: on magasine.

drills.en: I can't wait for the holidays!
I have a hard time understanding.
drills.why: avoir de la misère à = to have trouble.

a: C'est correct, y a pas de problème.
Ce n'est pas grave, pas de problème.
C'est pas grave, pas de problème.
drills.why: c'est correct is the Quebec go-to.

vocab.en: to be OK, to be alright
to go shopping; to shop around
to look forward to, can't wait

vocab.ex: J'ai de la misère à dormir.
Je ne suis pas du tout fatigué.

pron.tip: say-ko-RÈKT; Quebecers often say it fast: s'correct.
pahn-TOUTT: the final t is pronounced.
tee-ghee-DOO; hard g, with Quebec ts-like t.

dialogue.fr: Salut! On magasine samedi? Il y a des soldes au centre-ville.
dialogue.en: Hi! Shall we go shopping Saturday? There are sales downtown.

dialogue.fr: Bonne idée! J'ai besoin d'un manteau, je suis tanné de mon vieux.
dialogue.en: Good idea! I need a coat, I'm fed up with my old one.

dialogue.fr: On se rejoint à dix heures au métro?
dialogue.en: Meet at ten at the metro?

dialogue.fr: Tiguidou! Mais je vais être un peu en retard, désolé.
dialogue.en: Perfect! But I'm going to be a bit late, sorry.

dialogue.fr: C'est correct. Après, on jase au café?
dialogue.en: That's fine. After, we chat at the café?

dialogue.fr: Oui! J'ai hâte. La semaine est tellement plate.
dialogue.en: Yes! I can't wait. The week is so boring.
Are you mad at your boss?
Not at all! I'm just exhausted.

questions.q: What does B want to buy?
What does A say when B will be late?

speak.prompt: React to three situations: a friend is late, a friend asks if you're mad, a friend proposes a plan.
speak.model: C'est correct! / Pantoute! / Tiguidou, on fait ça!

speak.prompt: Say what you're fed up with and what you can't wait for.
speak.model: Je suis tanné de la neige. J'ai hâte à l'été!

speak.prompt: Say 'I'm going shopping on Saturday' in Quebec French, then the France way.
speak.model: Je vais magasiner samedi. / Je vais faire du shopping samedi.

write.prompt: Write a 5–6 line text message to a friend proposing a shopping trip, using at least four Quebec expressions from this lesson.
write.model: Salut! Je suis tanné de mes vieilles bottes. On magasine samedi? Il y a des soldes au centre-ville. Si t'es en retard, c'est correct. Après, on jase au café. J'ai hâte! Tiguidou?

quiz.why: France: faire du shopping / les magasins.

quiz.q: 'J'ai de la misère à dormir' means…
quiz.why: avoir de la misère à = to have a hard time.

quiz.q: Which expression is the MOST informal?
quiz.why: Pantoute is clearly informal; the others are neutral in Quebec.
Être brûlé = to be worn out; chu = je suis.
